title: Opinions & discussions
goal: Hold your own in a discussion: ask for and give opinions, agree and disagree politely, say 'it depends' and 'to be honest', talk about prices, politics and cricket, and use 'maybe / might / must be' and 'should have'.
intro:
Put three Sindhis round a pot of chai and you'll get four opinions — on the cricket, on prices, on the government, on whose biryani is best. This unit is about joining in: asking **توهان جي ڪهڙي راءِ آهي؟**, agreeing (**تون حق تي آهين**), disagreeing without offending (**ڳالهه ته صحيح آهي، پر…**), and hedging (**ٿي سگهي ٿو**، **مون کي يقين ناهي**).

Three pieces of grammar make you sound like you're really thinking: **probability** (شايد هو اچي 'he might come', هو گهر **هوندو** 'he must be at home'), **'I don't think…'** (مان **نٿو سمجهان** ته…), and **'should have'** (اسان کي جلدي نڪرڻ **گهرجي ها**).

grammar.title: Maybe, might, must be: talking about probability
grammar.body:
Sindhi has several ways to show how sure you are, from a wild guess to near-certainty.

**1. شايد 'perhaps' + subjunctive** (the present without ٿو) — 'might': **شايد** هو دير سان **اچي** 'he might come late'. With the future it sounds a little more likely: شايد هو **ايندو** 'he'll probably come'.

**2. ٿي سگهي ٿو ته + subjunctive** — 'it could be that…, maybe': **ٿي سگهي ٿو ته** سڀاڻي موڪل **هجي** 'there might be a holiday tomorrow'. On its own, **ٿي سگهي ٿو** = 'could be'.

**3. ممڪن آهي ته + subjunctive** — 'it's possible that…' (a bit more formal): ممڪن آهي ته هوءَ نوڪري ڇڏي **ڏئي**. Negative: **ڪو امڪان ناهي** 'there's no chance'.

**4. The future as a guess about now — 'must be'.** This is the most natural and most Sindhi way of guessing: use the **future of 'to be'** (هوندو، هوندي، هوندا) for something you think is true *right now*:
هو هن وقت آفيس ۾ **هوندو** — he'll be at the office now / he must be at the office
اهي ٿڪل **هوندا** — they must be tired
توهان کي بک لڳي **هوندي** — you must be hungry

**5. Certainty**: **ضرور** + future 'definitely will': هوءَ ضرور ايندي. **مون کي يقين آهي ته** … 'I'm sure that …'. Not sure: **مون کي يقين ناهي**.

**The subjunctive endings** (Unit 18): هو اچي، هوءَ اچي، اهي اچن، اسين اچون؛ هجڻ → هجي / هجن.

grammar.title: Disagreeing politely: 'I don't think…', 'it depends', 'to be honest'
grammar.body:
In Sindhi, as in English, a blunt **نه، غلط آهي** 'no, that's wrong' sounds rude except with very close friends. Discussion runs on softeners.

**I don't think…** — negate the *thinking*, just like English: **مان نٿو سمجهان ته** هو ايندو 'I don't think he'll come' (woman: **نٿي سمجهان**). You can also say **منهنجو خيال ناهي ته** …. Saying مان سمجهان ٿو ته هو نه ايندو is grammatical but sounds more definite.

**Agree, then disagree**: **ڳالهه ته صحيح آهي، پر…** 'that's true, but…' · **ٿي سگهي ٿو، پر…** 'could be, but…' · **توهان جي ڳالهه پنهنجي جاءِ تي، پر…** 'you have a point, but…'.

**Formal disagreement**: **مون کي … سان اختلاف آهي** 'I disagree with …' — polite, used with elders, at work, on TV. Add **معاف ڪجو، پر…** before it.

**It depends**: **… تي منحصر آهي** (اهو حالتن تي منحصر آهي) — or casually **ڏسڻو پوندو** 'we'll have to see'.

**To be honest**: **سچ ٻڌايان ته…** (very common) · **ايمانداريءَ سان چوان ته…** · **اصل ۾…** 'actually…' (Unit 20).

**Agreeing**: **تون حق تي آهين / توهان حق تي آهيو** 'you're right' · **بلڪل** · **مان متفق آهيان** (formal).

With friends, the friendly-rude register is fine and even affectionate: **ڇڏ يار، ڪهڙي ڳالهه ٿو ڪرين!** 'come off it, what are you on about!'.

grammar.title: 'Should have': infinitive + گهرجي ها
grammar.body:
You know **infinitive + گهرجي** for 'should' (Unit 9): توهان کي آرام ڪرڻ گهرجي 'you should rest'. To look back and say what **should have** happened (but didn't), add the little particle **ها** — the same ها that marks unreal conditions in Unit 19:

مون کي اچڻ **گهرجي ها** — I should have come
توهان کي فون ڪرڻ **گهرجي ها** — you should have called
پاڪستان کي اها ميچ کٽڻ **گهرجي ها** — Pakistan should have won that match

**Shouldn't have** = **نه** before the infinitive: هن کي اها ڳالهه **نه** چوڻ گهرجي ها 'he shouldn't have said that'.

The person still takes **کي** (it's the same 'to me it is necessary' construction), so the subject never changes form.

**Was supposed to** — use the -ṇo form (Unit 15) with the past of 'to be': مون کي ڪالهه **اچڻو هو** 'I was supposed to come yesterday', اسان کي ٽين وڳي **نڪرڻو هو** 'we were meant to leave at three'.

**If only… / If we had…** — for the full regret, combine with Unit 19's جيڪر … ها: **جيڪر** اسين ٽاس **کٽيون ها** ته ميچ به **کٽي وڃون ها** 'if we'd won the toss we'd have won the match'.

culture:
**Discussion is a pastime.** Sindhis love a good argument — at the dhaba, in the **اوطاق**, at family gatherings — and raised voices among friends don't mean anyone is angry. Cricket is the safest and most passionate topic: everyone is a selector and a captain, and a loss to India or Australia will be dissected for days. **مهانگائي** — the price of flour, sugar, petrol and electricity — is the universal complaint.

**Politics** is a national sport too, but tread carefully as a guest: listen more than you speak, don't take sides on parties or religion, and don't criticise Sindh or its heroes (Shah Abdul Latif, G.M. Syed, the Bhuttos) — people may criticise their own politicians freely, but not enjoy hearing it from an outsider. Safe phrases: **ٿي سگهي ٿو** 'could be', **اهو حالتن تي منحصر آهي** 'it depends', **مون کي گهڻي خبر ناهي** 'I don't know much about it'.

**Register**: with elders and at work, disagree with **معاف ڪجو، پر…** and **مون کي اختلاف آهي**; contradicting an older relative directly (**نه، توهان غلط آهيو**) is rude. Among friends, the opposite: too much politeness sounds cold, and **ڇڏ يار!** or **چريو آهين ڇا؟** is just part of the conversation. A discussion usually ends with a joke and more tea — **بحث ڇڏيو، چانهه پيئو!**

tip.title: What do you think?
tip.body:
- Ask: **توهان جي ڪهڙي راءِ آهي؟** · to a friend: **تون ڇا ٿو سمجهين؟**
- Give: **منهنجي خيال ۾** … · **منهنجي راءِ آهي ته** …
- Build the case: **مثال طور** 'for example', **ٻئي طرف** 'on the other hand'.
- راءِ is feminine: منهنجي راءِ، ڪهڙي راءِ.

tip.title: Might and maybe
tip.body:
- **شايد** + subjunctive (present without ٿو): **شايد** هو دير سان **اچي** 'he might come late'.
- **ٿي سگهي ٿو ته** + subjunctive: ٿي سگهي ٿو ته موڪل **هجي**.
- **ممڪن آهي ته** … = it's possible that …
- Sure: **مون کي يقين آهي ته** + future.
tip.pattern: شايد / ٿي سگهي ٿو ته + subjunctive

sentences.native: شايد هو دير سان اچي.
sentences.roman: shāyad hū dera sāṃ ache.
sentences.en: He might come late.

sentences.native: ٿي سگهي ٿو ته سڀاڻي موڪل هجي.
sentences.roman: thī saghe tho ta subhāṇe mokala huje.
sentences.en: There might be a holiday tomorrow.

sentences.native: ممڪن آهي ته هوءَ نوڪري ڇڏي ڏئي.
sentences.roman: mumkinu āhe ta hūa nokirī chhaɗī ɗie.
sentences.en: She may well quit her job.

sentences.native: مينهن پوڻ جو ڪو امڪان ناهي.
sentences.roman: mīṃhu pavaṇa jo ko imkānu nāhe.
sentences.en: There's no chance of rain.

sentences.native: مون کي يقين آهي ته هوءَ ضرور ايندي.
sentences.roman: moṃ khe yaqīnu āhe ta hūa zarūr endī.
sentences.en: I'm sure she'll come.

sentences.native: سڀ ڪجهه حالتن تي منحصر آهي.
sentences.roman: sabhu kujhu hālatan te munhasiru āhe.
sentences.en: Everything depends on the circumstances.

sentences.native: هن جي حالت ٺيڪ ناهي، شايد اسپتال وڃڻو پوي.
sentences.roman: hun jī hālata ṭhīku nāhe, shāyad ispatāla vañaṇo pave.
sentences.en: He's not in good shape — he might have to go to hospital.

sentences.native: شايد اسين ايندڙ مهيني ڪراچي وڃون.
sentences.roman: shāyad asīṃ endaṛa mahīne karāchī vañūṃ.
sentences.en: We might go to Karachi next month.

sentences.native: ٿي سگهي ٿو، پر مون کي يقين ناهي.
sentences.roman: thī saghe tho, para moṃ khe yaqīnu nāhe.
sentences.en: Could be, but I'm not sure.

tip.title: Must be: the future as a guess
tip.body:
- A guess about **now** uses the future of 'be': هو مصروف **هوندو** 'he must be busy', توهان کي بک لڳي **هوندي** 'you must be hungry'.
- A guess about the future: **شايد** + future: شايد اليڪشن جلد **ٿيندي**.
- Sure: **ضرور** + future.

sentences.native: شايد اليڪشن ايندڙ سال ٿيندي.
sentences.roman: shāyad elekshana endaṛa sāla thīndī.
sentences.en: The election will probably be next year.

sentences.native: مهانگائي ڏاڍي آهي، عوام پريشان آهي.
sentences.roman: mahāngāī ɗāḍhī āhe, ʿavāmu pareshānu āhe.
sentences.en: Prices are sky-high and people are struggling.

sentences.native: حڪومت ضرور نئون ٽيڪس لڳائيندي.
sentences.roman: hukūmata zarūr naoṃ ṭaiksu laɠāīndī.
sentences.en: The government's bound to bring in a new tax.

sentences.native: هن کي سياست جي سٺي خبر هوندي.
sentences.roman: hun khe siyāsata jī suṭhī xabara hundī.
sentences.en: He must know a lot about politics.

sentences.native: ماڻهو اڄ ووٽ ڏيڻ ويا هوندا.
sentences.roman: māṇhū aʄu voṭu ɗiyaṇa vayā hundā.
sentences.en: People must have gone to vote today.

sentences.native: نوجوانن کي ووٽ ضرور ڏيڻ گهرجي.
sentences.roman: naujavānan khe voṭu zarūr ɗiyaṇu ghurje.
sentences.en: Young people really should vote.

sentences.native: تعليم سڀ کان اهم آهي.
sentences.roman: taʿlīmu sabha khāṃ aham āhe.
sentences.en: Education is the most important thing.

sentences.native: عوام کي حڪومت تي يقين ناهي.
sentences.roman: ʿavāmu khe hukūmata te yaqīnu nāhe.
sentences.en: People don't trust the government.

sentences.native: اسين سياست تي ڳالهه نٿا ڪريون، رڳو بحث ٿئي ٿو!
sentences.roman: asīṃ siyāsata te ɠālhi nathā karyūṃ, raɠo bahasa thie tho!
sentences.en: We don't talk politics — it just turns into an argument!

sentences.native: ووٽ ڪنهن کي ڏيندين؟
sentences.roman: voṭu kanhin khe ɗīndeṃ?
sentences.en: Who are you going to vote for? (informal, to a man)

lessons.title: Looking back: what should have happened

tip.title: Should have = گهرجي ها
tip.body:
- Infinitive + **گهرجي ها**: مون کي اچڻ **گهرجي ها** 'I should have come'.
- Shouldn't have: **نه** + infinitive: هن کي اهو **نه** چوڻ گهرجي ها.
- Was supposed to: **-ṇo + هو**: مون کي اچڻو **هو**.
- The person takes **کي**.

new: پاڪستان کي اها ميچ کٽڻ گهرجي ها!
اسان کي اڳ ۾ ئي سوچڻ گهرجي ها.

sentences.native: مون کي توکي اڳ ۾ ئي ٻڌائڻ گهرجي ها.
sentences.roman: moṃ khe tokhe aɠa meṃ ī ɓudhāiṇu ghurje hā.
sentences.en: I should have told you earlier.

sentences.native: اسان کي جلدي نڪرڻ گهرجي ها، هاڻي ٽريفڪ ۾ ڦاسي پياسين.
sentences.roman: asāṃ khe jaldī nikiraṇu ghurje hā, hāṇe ṭraifika meṃ phāsī pyāsīṃ.
sentences.en: We should have left earlier — now we're stuck in traffic.

sentences.native: توهان کي پهريان فون ڪرڻ گهرجي ها.
sentences.roman: tavhāṃ khe pahiryāṃ fon karaṇu ghurje hā.
sentences.en: You should have called first.

sentences.native: هن کي اها ڳالهه نه چوڻ گهرجي ها.
sentences.roman: hun khe uhā ɠālhi na chavaṇu ghurje hā.
sentences.en: He shouldn't have said that.

sentences.native: ڪپتان کي پهريان بيٽنگ نه ڪرڻ گهرجي ها.
sentences.roman: kaptāna khe pahiryāṃ baiṭinga na karaṇu ghurje hā.
sentences.en: The captain shouldn't have batted first.

sentences.native: اسان کي ٽين وڳي نڪرڻو هو، پر دير ٿي وئي.
sentences.roman: asāṃ khe ṭīṃ vaɠe nikiraṇo ho, para dera thī vaī.
sentences.en: We were supposed to leave at three, but we got delayed.

sentences.native: اسان جو ڪپتان ڏاڍو هوشيار آهي.
sentences.roman: asāṃ jo kaptānu ɗāḍho hoshiyāru āhe.
sentences.en: Our captain is really sharp.

sentences.native: مون کي لڳي ٿو ته ايندڙ ميچ اسين کٽنداسين.
sentences.roman: moṃ khe laɠe tho ta endaṛa mecha asīṃ khaṭandāsīṃ.
sentences.en: I think we'll win the next match.

sentences.native: جيڪر اسين ٽاس کٽيون ها ته ميچ به کٽي وڃون ها.
sentences.roman: jekar asīṃ ṭāsa khaṭyūṃ hā ta mecha bi khaṭī vañūṃ hā.
sentences.en: If we'd won the toss, we'd have won the match too.
